akhfash:7-7.t: He said ﴿وَٱلسَّمَآءِ ذَاتِ ٱلْحُبُكِ﴾: its singular is "الحِباك" (pathway, streak).

akhfash:12-13.t: And He said ﴿أَيَّانَ يَوْمُ ٱلدِّينِ﴾ ﴿يَوْمَ هُمْ عَلَى ٱلنَّارِ يُفْتَنُونَ﴾, i.e. when is the Day of Judgement? And it was said to them: on the day when they are tried over the Fire. Because that day is a long day, in which is the reckoning and in which is their trial over the Fire.

akhfash:59-59.t: And He said ﴿ذَنُوباً مِّثْلَ ذَنُوبِ أَصْحَابِهِمْ﴾, i.e. a bucketful (سَجْلاً) of punishment.

daas-irab:1-12.t: ﴿وَالذَّارِياتِ﴾ the wāw is a particle of oath and genitive, and الذاريات is the thing sworn by, genitive (majrūr); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb of swearing. ﴿ذَرْواً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause is initial and has no grammatical position. ﴿فَالْحامِلاتِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الذاريات. ﴿وِقْراً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the active participle. ﴿فَالْجارِياتِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿يُسْراً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فَالْمُقَسِّماتِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَمْراً﴾ mafʿūl bihi of the active participle. ﴿إِنَّما﴾ inna is a particle resembling the verb, and mā is its noun. ﴿تُوعَدُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿لَصادِقٌ﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and صادق is the khabar (predicate) of inna; the nominal clause is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَإِنَّ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and inna is a particle resembling the verb. ﴿الدِّينَ﴾ its noun. ﴿لَواقِعٌ﴾ the shifted lām, and واقع is the khabar of inna; the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَالسَّماءِ﴾ the wāw is a particle of oath and genitive, and السماء is genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "أقسم". ﴿ذاتِ﴾ an adjective of السماء. ﴿الْحُبُكِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿إِنَّكُمْ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿لَفِي قَوْلٍ﴾ the shifted lām, and a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted khabar of inna. ﴿مُخْتَلِفٍ﴾ an adjective of قول; the nominal clause is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position. ﴿يُؤْفَكُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb. ﴿عَنْهُ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿مَنْ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil. ﴿أُفِكَ﴾ a passive past verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila of man, and the clause يؤفك is resumptive. ﴿قُتِلَ﴾ a passive past verb. ﴿الْخَرَّاصُونَ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ) by the wāw; the clause is resumptive. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a badal (substitute) from الخراصون. ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿فِي غَمْرَةٍ﴾ the two are attached to what follows them. ﴿ساهُونَ﴾ khabar; the nominal clause is the ṣila of الذين and has no grammatical position. ﴿يَسْئَلُونَ﴾ a nominative imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent). ﴿أَيَّانَ﴾ an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as an adverbial of time, attached to an omitted, advanced khabar. ﴿يَوْمُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿الدِّينِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the nominal clause stands in place of the two objects of يسألون, and the verbal clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:13-20.t: ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿عَلَى النَّارِ﴾ the two (preposition and genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) what follows them. ﴿يُفْتَنُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the deputy (nāʾib); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of هم, and the nominal clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿ذُوقُوا﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the object of an omitted saying. ﴿فِتْنَتَكُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿هذَا﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿الَّذِي﴾ its khabar; the nominal clause is an explanation of cause (taʿlīl). ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿بِهِ﴾ the two are attached to what follows them. ﴿تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of كنتم, and the clause كنتم is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذي and has no grammatical position. ﴿إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿فِي جَنَّاتٍ﴾ its khabar. ﴿وَعُيُونٍ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to جنات. ﴿آخِذِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi of آخذين. ﴿آتاهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl. ﴿رَبُّهُمْ﴾ its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِنَّهُمْ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun; the verbal clause is the khabar of inna. ﴿قَبْلَ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿مُحْسِنِينَ﴾ the khabar of كانوا; the nominal clause is an explanation of cause. ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿قَلِيلًا﴾ an adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿مِنَ اللَّيْلِ﴾ the two are attached to قليلا. ﴿ما﴾ redundant (zāʾida). ﴿يَهْجَعُونَ﴾ a nominative imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the verbal clause is the khabar of كانوا, and the clause كانوا is a badal (substitute) from the one before it. ﴿وَبِالْأَسْحارِ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and بالأسحار: the two are attached to يستغفرون. ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ﴾ a nominative imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the verbal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿وَفِي أَمْوالِهِمْ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted, advanced khabar. ﴿حَقٌّ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿لِلسَّائِلِ﴾ the two are attached to حق. ﴿وَالْمَحْرُومِ﴾ conjoined to السائل; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَفِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted, advanced khabar. ﴿آياتٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿لِلْمُوقِنِينَ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted adjective of آيات; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:21-27.t: ﴿وَفِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and في أنفسكم: the two (preposition and genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "آيات". ﴿أَفَلا﴾ the hamza is for interrogation, the fāʾ is a particle of resumption, and lā is negating. ﴿تُبْصِرُونَ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the verbal clause is resumptive. ﴿وَفِي السَّماءِ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and في السماء is an advanced khabar. ﴿رِزْقُكُمْ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَما﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to رزقكم. ﴿تُوعَدُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of mā and has no grammatical position. ﴿فَوَ رَبِّ﴾ the fāʾ is a particle of resumption, the wāw is a particle of oath and genitive, and رب is genitive by the wāw. ﴿السَّماءِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined to السماء. ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿لَحَقٌّ﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and حق is its khabar; the nominal clause is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position. ﴿مِثْلَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb). ﴿ما﴾ redundant (zāʾida). ﴿أَنَّكُمْ﴾ anna and its noun. ﴿تَنْطِقُونَ﴾ a nominative imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the verbal clause is the khabar of anna, and the nominal clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿هَلْ﴾ a particle of interrogation. ﴿أَتاكَ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl (object). ﴿حَدِيثُ﴾ its fāʿil. ﴿ضَيْفِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿إِبْراهِيمَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿الْمُكْرَمِينَ﴾ an adjective of ضيف; the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿دَخَلُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿فَقالُوا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿سَلاماً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿سَلامٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted; the nominal clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿قَوْمٌ﴾ the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. ﴿مُنْكَرُونَ﴾ an adjective of قوم; the nominal clause is the object of saying. ﴿فَراغَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿إِلى أَهْلِهِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿فَجاءَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿بِعِجْلٍ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿سَمِينٍ﴾ an adjective of عجل; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَقَرَّبَهُ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿أَلا﴾ a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ). ﴿تَأْكُلُونَ﴾ a nominative imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the object of saying, and the clause قال is a ḥāl.

daas-irab:28-30.t: ﴿فَأَوْجَسَ﴾ the fāʾ is a particle of resumption, and a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿خِيفَةً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive. ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿لا تَخَفْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lā, and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَبَشَّرُوهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl; the clause is conjoined to قالوا. ﴿بِغُلامٍ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿عَلِيمٍ﴾ an adjective. ﴿فَأَقْبَلَتِ﴾ a conjunction and a past verb. ﴿امْرَأَتُهُ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿فِي صَرَّةٍ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فَصَكَّتْ﴾ a conjunction and a past verb. ﴿وَجْهَها﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined to أقبلت. ﴿وَقالَتْ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿عَجُوزٌ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿عَقِيمٌ﴾ an adjective of عجوز; the nominal clause is the object of saying. ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿كَذلِكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿قالَ رَبُّكِ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the object of saying. ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿هُوَ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿الْحَكِيمُ الْعَلِيمُ﴾ two predicates; the nominal clause is the object of saying.

daas-irab:31-33.t: ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَما﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (fāʾ of elucidation), and mā is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿خَطْبُكُمْ﴾ khabar (predicate); the clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿أَيُّهَا﴾ the one addressed (munādā). ﴿الْمُرْسَلُونَ﴾ a badal (substitute) from أي; the clause قال is resumptive. ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿أُرْسِلْنا﴾ a passive past verb, and nā is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the khabar of inna. ﴿إِلى قَوْمٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿مُجْرِمِينَ﴾ an adjective; the nominal clause is the object of saying. ﴿لِنُرْسِلَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an concealed after the lām of causation, and the fāʿil is latent. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿حِجارَةً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿مِنْ طِينٍ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted adjective of حجارة; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from an and what follows it is in the position of the genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أرسلنا.

daas-irab:34-39.t: ﴿مُسَوَّمَةً﴾ a second adjective of حجارة. ﴿عِنْدَ﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿لِلْمُسْرِفِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) مسومة. ﴿فَأَخْرَجْنا﴾ the fāʾ is a particle of resumption, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿مَنْ﴾ its mafʿūl (object); the clause is resumptive. ﴿كانَ﴾ an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is omitted. ﴿فِيها﴾ the two are attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of kāna. ﴿مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause of kāna is the ṣila (relative clause) of man. ﴿فَما﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and mā is negating. ﴿وَجَدْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿فِيها﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿غَيْرَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿بَيْتٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ﴾ an adjective of بيت; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَتَرَكْنا﴾ a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿فِيها﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿آيَةً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted adjective of آية. ﴿يَخافُونَ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿الْعَذابَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الْأَلِيمَ﴾ an adjective; the clause يخافون is the ṣila of الذين. ﴿وَفِي مُوسى﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and the preposition and its genitive noun are conjoined to فيها. ﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿أَرْسَلْناهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿إِلى فِرْعَوْنَ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿بِسُلْطانٍ﴾ the two are also attached to the verb. ﴿مُبِينٍ﴾ an adjective. ﴿فَتَوَلَّى﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿بِرُكْنِهِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿وَقالَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿ساحِرٌ﴾ the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿أَوْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿مَجْنُونٌ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ساحر; the clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl).

daas-irab:40-44.t: [Translator's note: at the start of this entry the source text is garbled: the quotation brackets and the first letters of the Quranic words are lost (it reads «َأَخَذْناهُ», «جُنُودَهُ», «نَبَذْناهُمْ», «ِي الْيَمِّ», «هُوَ», «ُلِيمٌ»). The words are restored below from the Quranic text of the verse, ﴿فَأَخَذْناهُ وَجُنُودَهُ فَنَبَذْناهُمْ فِي الْيَمِّ وَهُوَ مُلِيمٌ﴾.] ﴿فَأَخَذْناهُ﴾ a conjunction, and a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl (object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَجُنُودَهُ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the pronoun, so it is accusative (manṣūb) like it. ﴿فَنَبَذْناهُمْ﴾ a conjunction, and a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فِي الْيَمِّ﴾ the two (preposition and genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿وَهُوَ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿مُلِيمٌ﴾ its khabar (predicate); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَفِي عادٍ إِذْ أَرْسَلْنا﴾ its i'rab has preceded. ﴿عَلَيْهِمُ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿الرِّيحَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿الْعَقِيمَ﴾ an adjective. ﴿ما تَذَرُ﴾ mā is negating, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿مِنْ شَيْءٍ﴾ min is a redundant (zāʾid) preposition, and a noun genitive in form, accusative in position, the object of تذر. ﴿أَتَتْ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb; the clause is an adjective of شيء. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿جَعَلَتْهُ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl, and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is in the position of the accusative as a second mafʿūl bihi of تذر. ﴿كَالرَّمِيمِ﴾ the kāf, in the sense of مثل ("like"), is the second mafʿūl bihi of جعلته, and الرميم is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause ما تذر is a ḥāl. ﴿وَفِي ثَمُودَ إِذْ﴾ the i'rab of its like has preceded. ﴿قِيلَ﴾ a passive past verb. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿تَمَتَّعُوا﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿حَتَّى حِينٍ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿فَعَتَوْا﴾ a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to قيل. ﴿فَأَخَذَتْهُمُ الصَّاعِقَةُ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl, and الصاعقة is its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to عتوا. ﴿وَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial, and هم is a mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَنْظُرُونَ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is a ḥāl.

daas-irab:45-51.t: ﴿فَمَا﴾ the fāʾ is a particle of resumption, and mā is negating. ﴿اسْتَطاعُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿مِنْ قِيامٍ﴾ min is a redundant (zāʾid) preposition, and a noun genitive in form, accusative in position, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَما﴾ a conjunction, and mā is negating. ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿مُنْتَصِرِينَ﴾ its khabar (predicate); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَقَوْمَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and قوم is accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muqaddar) verb, أهلكنا. ﴿نُوحٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ the two (preposition and genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied verb. ﴿إِنَّهُمْ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿قَوْماً﴾ its khabar; the verbal clause is the khabar of inna. ﴿فاسِقِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); the nominal clause is an explanation of cause (taʿlīl). [Translator's note: so in the source; فاسقين is more usually parsed as an adjective of قوما.] ﴿وَالسَّماءَ﴾ the wāw is a particle of resumption, and السماء is accusative by way of ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb), its implied form being "بنينا السماء"; the verbal clause is resumptive. ﴿بَنَيْناها﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl. ﴿بِأَيْدٍ﴾ the two are attached to the verb; the clause is explicative of the implied clause and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَإِنَّا﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and inna and its noun. ﴿لَمُوسِعُونَ﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and the khabar of inna; the nominal clause is a ḥāl. ﴿وَالْأَرْضَ فَرَشْناها﴾ conjoined to السماء بنيناها. ﴿فَنِعْمَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for expressing praise. ﴿الْماهِدُونَ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿وَمِنْ كُلِّ﴾ the wāw is a particle of resumption, and a preposition and its genitive noun attached to خلقنا. ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿خَلَقْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿زَوْجَيْنِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ﴾ laʿalla and its noun. ﴿تَذَكَّرُونَ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of laʿalla, and the nominal clause is explanatory of cause and has no grammatical position. ﴿فَفِرُّوا﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (fāʾ of elucidation), and an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿إِلَى اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, genitive by ilā, and the two are attached to the verb; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition and has no grammatical position. ﴿إِنِّي﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ the two are attached to نذير. ﴿مِنْهُ﴾ the two are also attached to نذير. ﴿نَذِيرٌ﴾ the khabar of inna. ﴿مُبِينٌ﴾ an adjective; the nominal clause is an explanation of cause. ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and lā is prohibitive. ﴿تَجْعَلُوا﴾ a jussive (majzūm) imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿مَعَ﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿إِلهاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿آخَرَ﴾ an adjective of it; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿إِنِّي لَكُمْ مِنْهُ نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ its i'rab has preceded.

daas-irab:52-55.t: ﴿كَذلِكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿ما﴾ negating. ﴿أَتَى الَّذِينَ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl (object). ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿مِنْ رَسُولٍ﴾ a redundant (zāʾid) preposition, and a noun genitive in form, nominative in position, the fāʿil (agent) of أتى. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿ساحِرٌ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿أَوْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿مَجْنُونٌ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ساحر; the clause قالوا is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the clause ما أتى is explicative (tafsīriyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿أَتَواصَوْا﴾ the hamza is a particle of interrogation and rebuke, and a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿بِهِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb; the clause is resumptive. ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of conjunction and digression (iḍrāb). ﴿هُمْ قَوْمٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar. ﴿طاغُونَ﴾ an adjective of قوم; the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَتَوَلَّ﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (fāʾ of elucidation), and an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the weak letter; the fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿عَنْهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to the verb; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition and has no grammatical position. ﴿فَما﴾ the fāʾ is a particle of causation, and mā is negating, operating like laysa. ﴿أَنْتَ﴾ its noun. ﴿بِمَلُومٍ﴾ the bāʾ is a redundant preposition, and ملوم is genitive in form, accusative in position, because it is the khabar of mā; the clause is explanatory of cause (taʿlīliyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَذَكِّرْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿فَإِنَّ الذِّكْرى﴾ the fāʾ is a particle of causation, and inna and its noun. ﴿تَنْفَعُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the verbal clause is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is explanatory of cause and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:56-60.t: ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a particle of resumption, and mā is negating. ﴿خَلَقْتُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿الْجِنَّ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَالْإِنْسَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الجن; the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿لِيَعْبُدُونِ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an concealed after the lām of consequence (lām al-ʿāqiba); the wāw is its fāʿil, the nūn is for protection (wiqāya), and the omitted yāʾ of the speaker is mafʿūl bihi; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from an and what follows it is in the position of the genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) خلقت. ﴿ما﴾ negating. ﴿أُرِيدُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿مِنْ رِزْقٍ﴾ min is a redundant (zāʾid) preposition, and رزق is genitive in form, accusative in position, mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَما أُرِيدُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and ما أريد is conjoined to its like. ﴿أَنْ يُطْعِمُونِ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative by an; the wāw is its fāʿil, the nūn is for protection, and the omitted yāʾ of the speaker is mafʿūl bihi; the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and what follows it is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi of أريد. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ inna, and the Name of Majesty is its noun. ﴿هُوَ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿الرَّزَّاقُ﴾ its khabar (predicate); the clause هو الرزاق is the khabar of inna, and the clause إن الله is resumptive. ﴿ذُو﴾ a second khabar. ﴿الْقُوَّةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿الْمَتِينُ﴾ an adjective of الرزاق. ﴿فَإِنَّ﴾ the fāʾ is a particle of resumption, and a particle resembling the verb. ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾ the advanced khabar of inna. ﴿ظَلَمُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿ذَنُوباً﴾ the postponed noun of inna. ﴿مِثْلَ﴾ an adjective of ذنوبا. ﴿ذَنُوبِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَصْحابِهِمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَلا﴾ a conjunction, and lā is prohibitive. ﴿يَسْتَعْجِلُونِ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lā; the wāw is its fāʿil, the nūn is for protection, and the omitted yāʾ of the speaker is mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فَوَيْلٌ﴾ a particle of resumption, and a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾ khabar; the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿مِنْ يَوْمِهِمُ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted adjective of ويل. ﴿الَّذِي﴾ an adjective of يومهم. ﴿يُوعَدُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the ṣila.

farraa:18-18.t: His saying: ﴿وَبِٱلأَسْحَارِ هُمْ يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ﴾: they pray.

farraa:19-19.t:
His saying: ﴿وَفِيۤ أَمْوَالِهِمْ حَقٌّ لَّلسَّآئِلِ وَٱلْمَحْرُومِ﴾.
As for «السائل» (the one who asks), it is the one who goes round from door to door; as for «المحروم» (the deprived), it is the one denied his livelihood (al-muḥāraf), or the one who has no share in the spoils.

farraa:20-20.t:
His saying: ﴿وَفِي ٱلأَرْضِ آيَاتٌ لِّلْمُوقِنِينَ﴾.
The signs of the earth are its mountains, the variety of its plants and its rivers, and the creatures that are in it.

farraa:21-21.t:
His saying: ﴿وَفِيۤ أَنفُسِكُمْ﴾.
There are signs too: one of you eats and drinks through a single entrance and excretes from two places. Then He rebuked them, saying: ﴿أَفَلاَ تُبْصِرُونَ﴾ (Will you not then see?)

farraa:23-23.t:
His saying: ﴿فَوَرَبِّ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
He, Mighty and Majestic, swore by Himself that what I have told you is truly the truth, just as (مثل ما أنكم) you speak. Someone may ask: how have «ما» and «أنّ» come together, when one of them suffices for the other? There are two answers to this. The first is that the Arabs combine two things, both among nouns and among particles (adawāt), when their wording differs. Among nouns there is the poet's saying:
من النّفر اللائى الذين إذا همُ * يَهاب اللئامُ حلقهَ البابِ قَعْقَعوا
(Of the band who — who, when the base fear the door-knocker, rattle it.) So he combined «اللائى» and «الذين», though each of them suffices for the other.
As for particles, there is the saying:
ما إِنْ رأيتُ ولا سمعت به * كاليوم طالى أيْنُق جُرْب
(I have never seen nor heard of anything like today: one tarring mangy she-camels.) So he combined «ما» and «إن», both of which are negations (jaḥd), one of which suffices for the other.
As for the other answer: if the meaning had been expressed with «ما» alone, it would be as though speech in itself were true and not a lie, and that is not what was meant. What they meant is only that it is true just as it is true that a human being speaks.
Do you not see that your saying «أحقٌّ منطقك» (Is your speech true?) means: is it true or a lie? And that your saying «أحقٌّ أنك تنطق؟» (Is it true that you speak?) means: does speech belong to man and not to others? So you introduced «أنَّ» in order to distinguish thereby between the two meanings. This is the one of the two answers I prefer.
ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash read (مثلَ) in the nominative (rafʿ), while the people of the Hijaz and al-Ḥasan read it in the accusative (naṣb). Whoever read it in the nominative made it a naʿt (adjective) of «الحق»; whoever read it in the accusative put it in the manner of the maṣdar (verbal noun), as when you say: «إنه لحق حقا» (It is truly true). And the Arabs put it in the accusative even when the noun is made nominative by it, saying: «مثلَ من عبدالله؟» (Like whom is ʿAbd Allāh?), and they say: «عبدالله [185/ا] مثلَك» (ʿAbd Allāh is like you), and «أنت مثلَه» (You are like him). The reason for its accusative is that the kāf (of comparison) may enter upon it, so it is put in the accusative when the kāf is dropped. If someone asks: may one then say «زيدٌ الأسدَ شدةً» (Zayd is the lion in strength), putting «الأسد» in the accusative when you drop the kāf? I say: no; that is because «مثلَ» stands in place of the kāf, whereas «الأسد» does not stand in place of it. Do you not see, in the poet's saying:
وزعتُ بكالهراوة أعوجِىٍّ * إذا وَنتِ الرِّكاب جرى وثابا
(I held them back on one like a cudgel, an Aʿwajī steed, who, when the riding camels flag, runs leaping.)
that the kāf has sufficed in place of «مثل»? And the Arabs combine the two, saying: «زيد كمثلك» (Zayd is like the like of you); and Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿ليس كمثله شىء وهو السميع البصير﴾. Their coming together is evidence that their meaning is one, just as I told you about «ما» and «إن» and «لا» and others.

farraa:24-24.t:
His saying: ﴿هَلْ أَتَاكَ حَدِيثُ ضَيْفِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ﴾.
The Prophet ﷺ did not know of it until Allah revealed it to him.
And His saying: ﴿ٱلْمُكْرَمِينَ﴾.
He honoured them by the deed that brought him near.

farraa:25-25.t:
His saying: ﴿قَوْمٌ مُّنكَرُونَ﴾.
It is nominative (marfūʿ) by an implied pronoun: «أنتم قوم منكرون» (You are a people unknown).
This is said by Abraham, peace be upon him, to the angels.

farraa:26-26.t:
His saying: ﴿فَرَاغَ إِلَىٰ أَهْلِهِ﴾.
He returned to them. Although «الروغ» has this meaning, it is not used unless the one doing it conceals his going [or his coming]. Do you not see that you do not say «قد راغ أهل مكة» (the people of Mecca have slipped away) when you mean they returned or came back? But if a returner concealed his return, «راغ» and «يروغ» would be fitting for it.

farraa:28-28.t:
His saying: ﴿وَبَشَّرُوهُ بِغُلاَمٍ عَلَيمٍ﴾.
That is, when he grows up. One of our elders used to say: when knowledge is still awaited [for one] who is described by it, you say of the «عليم» who does not yet know: «إنه لعالم عن قيل» (he will be knowing shortly) and «فاقِهٌ» (understanding); of the lord («السيد»): «سائد», and of the generous («الكريم»): «كارم». What he said is good, and this is good Arabic speech; yet Allah has said it with «عليم», «حليم» and «ميت».
The elders used to say of one who has not yet died but will die: «هو مائت عن قليل» (he will be dying shortly); but the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is more correct than their saying. Among what they adduced as evidence is the poet's saying:
كريم كصفو الماء ليس بباخل * بشىء، ولا مهد ملاما لباخل
(Generous, like clear water, not stingy with anything, nor one who directs blame at a stingy man.)
He means «بخيل» (stingy), but he made it «باخل» because he has not yet been stingy.

farraa:29-29.t:
His saying: ﴿فَأَقْبَلَتِ ٱمْرَأَتُهُ فِي صَرَّةٍ﴾.
In a cry. She did not come forward from one place to another; it is only like your saying: «أقبل يشتمنى» (he set about insulting me), i.e. he began insulting me. They have mentioned that the cry was «أوَّه» (Ah!), and some said it was «يا ويلتا» (Woe is me!).
And His saying: ﴿فَصَكَّتْ وَجْهَهَا﴾.
Like this, that is, she gathered her fingers and struck her forehead; ﴿وَقَالَتْ عَجُوزٌ عَقِيمٌ﴾: will a barren old woman give birth? You make it nominative by the implied (verb) «تلد».
«[Translator's note: the source has «بالضيمر», evidently a slip for «بالضمير» (by the implied element).]»

farraa:37-37.t:
His saying: ﴿وَتَرَكْنَا فِيهَآ آيَةً﴾.
Its meaning is: We left it as a sign; just as you say of the sky «فيها آية» (in it is a sign), meaning that it is itself the sign.

farraa:39-39.t:
His saying: ﴿فَتَوَلَّىٰ بِرُكْنِهِ﴾.
It is said: «تولى» means he turned away from the Reminder by the strength he had in himself; and it is said: «فتولى بركنه» means with those who were with him, because they were his strength.

farraa:40-40.t:
His saying: ﴿وَهُوَ مُلِيمٌ﴾.
He did what deserves blame; one says «قد ألام» (he has become blameworthy). And His saying: ﴿لَقَدْ كَانَ فِى يُوسُفَ وَإِخْوَتِهِ آياتٌ لِلسّائِلِينَ﴾: they are the signs, they and their deeds.

farraa:42-42.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿كَٱلرَّمِيمِ﴾.
«الرميم» is the vegetation of the earth when it dries and withers (dabisa); then it is «رميم».

farraa:43-43.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿تَمَتَّعُواْ حَتَّىٰ حِينٍ﴾.
That «حين» (period) was three days.

farraa:44-44.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿فَأَخَذَتْهُمُ ٱلصَّاعِقَةُ﴾.
The generality of readers read it [الصاعقة] with the alif.
He said: Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm told us: al-Farrāʾ told us: Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ told me, from al-Suddī, from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, that he read (الصَّعقة) without the alif, «وهم ينظرون».

farraa:45-45.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَمَا ٱسْتَطَاعُواْ مِن قِيَامٍ﴾.
He is saying: they did not stand up against it. Had it been «فما استطاعُوا من إقامةٍ», it would have been correct.
Dropping the alif from it is like His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿والله أَنْبَتَكُم مِنَ الأَرْضِ نَبَاتاً﴾; had it been «إنباتا», it would have been correct.

farraa:46-46.t:
His saying, exalted be His mention: ﴿وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ﴾.
The readers put it in the accusative [55/ا], except al-Aʿmash and his companions, who put it in the genitive (khafḍ), because in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh, as far as I know, it is: «وفى قوم نوح» (and in the people of Noah).
Whoever puts it in the accusative does so in one of two ways: the thunderbolt seized them and seized the people of Noah;
or, if you wish: We destroyed them and destroyed the people of Noah. There is another way, no less dear to me than these two: that you imply a verb — «and mention to them the people of Noah» — as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَإِبْرَاهِيمَ إِذْ قَالَ لِقَوْمِهِ﴾ and ﴿وَنُوحاً إِذْ نَادَى مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ in many places in the Quran, its meaning being: inform them and mention to them the prophets and their stories.

farraa:47-47.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿بِأَييْدٍ﴾: with strength.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَإِنَّا لَمُوسِعُونَ﴾, that is: We are possessed of ample means for Our creation. Likewise His saying, exalted be His mention: ﴿عَلَى الْمُوسِعِ قَدَرُهُ﴾.
«[Translator's note: the source has «لدو», evidently for «لذو» (possessors of).]»

farraa:49-49.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿وَمِن كُلِّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقْنَا زَوْجَيْنِ﴾.
The pairs among all animals are the male and the female; and among other things: the different colours of plants and the tastes of fruits, some sweet and some sour — those are two pairs.

farraa:50-50.t:
His saying: ﴿فَفِرُّوۤاْ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ﴾.
Its meaning is: flee to Him, to obedience to Him, away from disobeying Him.

farraa:53-53.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿أَتَوَاصَوْاْ بِهِ﴾.
Its meaning is: did the people of Mecca [55/ب] and the past nations bequeath it to one another, since they said to you what the nations said to their messengers?

farraa:56-56.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿وَمَا خَلَقْتُ ٱلْجِنَّ وَٱلإِنسَ إِلاَّ لِيَعْبُدُونِ﴾.
Except that they should affirm My oneness; and this is specific. He is saying: I did not create the people of felicity among the two groups except that they should affirm My oneness.
Some said: He created them so that they would do (this); some of them did and some left it. There is no argument in it for the people of qadar (the Qadarites); and it has (already) been explained.

farraa:57-58.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿مَآ أُرِيدُ مِنْهُم مِّن رِّزْقٍ﴾.
He is saying: I do not want them to provide for themselves; ﴿وَمَآ أُرِيدُ أَن يُطْعِمُونِ﴾: that they should feed any of My creation. ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلرَّزَّاقُ ذُو ٱلْقُوَّةِ ٱلْمَتِينُ﴾.
Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read (المتين) in the genitive, making it a naʿt (adjective) of «القوة»; even though it is feminine in form, he took it in the sense of the rope and of a twisted thing.
One of the Arabs recited:
لكل دَهْرٍ قد لَبِسْتُ أثْوباً * من ريطةٍ وَاليُمنَةَ المُعَصَّبا
(For every age I have worn garments: of fine sheets, and the striped Yemeni cloth.) He made «المُعَصَّب» a naʿt of «اليُمْنَة», which is feminine in form, because «اليُمنة» is a kind and type of garment, namely embroidered cloth (al-washy), so he took it in that sense.
The people read (المتينُ) in the nominative, as a description of Allah, Blessed and Exalted.

farraa:59-59.t:
His saying [56/ا], Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَإِنَّ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ ذَنُوباً﴾.
«الذنوب» in the speech of the Arabs is the large bucket, but the Arabs take it in the sense of share and portion.
The exegesis came in that sense: those who did wrong will have a portion of punishment, as befell those before them. The poet said:
لنَا ذَنوبٌ وَلكمْ ذَنوبُ * فإنْ أبيتمْ فلنا القَليبُ
(We have a bucketful and you have a bucketful; if you refuse, then the well is ours.)
«الذنوب» is treated as both masculine and feminine.

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَٱلذَّارِيَاتِ ذَرْواً﴾.
He means: the winds.

farraa:2-2.t: ﴿فَٱلْحَامِلاَتِ وِقْراً﴾: He means: the clouds, because they carry the water.

farraa:3-4.t:
﴿فَٱلْجَارِيَاتِ يُسْراً﴾: they are the ships that run with ease. ﴿فَٱلْمُقَسِّمَاتِ أَمْراً﴾: the angels who come with differing commands: Gabriel, master of severity (ghilẓa), Michael, master of mercy, and the Angel of Death, who comes with death. That is the apportioning of affairs.
«[Translator's note: the source has «الغلطة» ("error"), evidently for «الغلظة» ("severity"); translated as "severity".]»

farraa:7-7.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلسَّمَآءِ ذَاتِ ٱلْحُبُكِ﴾.
Al-ḥubuk is the rippling of anything, like the sand when a gentle wind passes over it, and standing water when the wind passes over it; and the coat of mail, the iron coat of mail, also has ḥubuk; and the curly hair, its waves are ḥubuk. The singular of ḥubuk is ḥibāk and ḥabīka.

farraa:8-8.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّكُمْ لَفِي قَوْلٍ مُّخْتَلِفٍ﴾.
The answer to the oath. The differing speech is the denial by some of them of the Qurʾān and of Muḥammad, and the faith of others.

farraa:9-9.t:
His saying: ﴿يُؤْفَكُ عَنْهُ مَنْ أُفِكَ﴾.
He means: he is turned away from the Qurʾān and faith who is turned away, as He said: ﴿أَجِئْتَنَا لِتَأْفِكَنَا﴾: he says: to turn us away from our gods and to bar us.

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying: ﴿قُتِلَ ٱلْخَرَّاصُونَ﴾.
He says: cursed be the liars who said that Muḥammad, Allah bless him, is mad, a poet, a liar, a sorcerer. They conjectured (kharraṣū) about what they had no knowledge of.

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَ أَيَّانَ يَوْمُ ٱلدِّينِ﴾.
"When is the Day of Judgement?" Allah said: ﴿يوم الدّين. يَوْمَ هُمْ على النارِ يُفْتَنُون﴾. You put (يومَ هُمْ) in the accusative only because you annexed it to two things [i.e. a nominal clause]. When "day" and "night" are annexed to a noun that has a verb [i.e. a predicate], and both are nominative, "day" is accusative, even if it is in the position of the genitive or the nominative. When it is annexed to faʿala or yafʿalu or the like, then its nominative in the position of the nominative, and its genitive in the position of the genitive, are allowed. So had it been said: يومُ هم على النار يفتنون, putting يوم in the nominative, it would have been a valid view, but none of the readers read it so.

farraa:13-13.t: His saying: ﴿يُفْتَنُونَ﴾: they are burned and punished with the Fire.

farraa:14-14.t: His saying: ﴿ذُوقُواْ فِتْنَتَكُمْ﴾: he says: taste your punishment which you used to seek to hasten in the world.

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying: ﴿آخِذِينَ﴾ and "وفاكهين".
They are accusative by detachment (qaṭʿ, i.e. as ḥāl); and had they been [184/b] nominative, it would have been correct: their nominative being as a khabar (predicate); and another nominative is also [possible] by resumption (istiʾnāf).

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿كَانُواْ قَلِيلاً مِّن ٱللَّيْلِ مَا يَهْجَعُونَ﴾.
If you wish, you put ما in the position of the nominative, and the meaning is: their slumber was little. Al-hujūʿ is sleep.
And if you wish, you make ما a connective (ṣila) with no position, and put قليلا in the accusative by يهجعون, meaning: they used to sleep a little of the night.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat "al-Dhāriyāt".
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿والذّارِياتِ ذَرْوًا﴾: It has come in the tafsīr (exegesis) from ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, that Ibn al-Kawwāʾ asked him about ﴿والذّارِياتِ ذَرْوًا﴾, and ʿAlī said: "They are the winds." He said: ﴿فالحامِلاتِ وِقْرًا﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 2]? He said: "The clouds." He said: ﴿فالجارِياتِ يُسْرًا﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 3]? He said: "The ships." He said: ﴿فالمُقَسِّماتِ أمْرًا﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 4]? He said: "The angels." And all the exegetes hold ʿAlī's view on this.
[Translator's note: the source reads «الكَوّاءَ»; the questioner is usually named ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Kawwāʾ.]
﴿والذّارِياتِ﴾ is genitive (majrūr) by the oath; the meaning is: "I swear by the scattering winds" and by these things, and the answer is: ﴿إنَّما تُوعَدُونَ لَصادِقٌ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 5]. Some said: the meaning is: "and by the Lord of the scattering winds", as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَوَرَبِّ السَّماءِ والأرْضِ إنَّهُ لَحَقٌّ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 23]. "اَلذّارِياتُ" is from "ذَرَتِ الرِّيحُ، تَذْرُو", when the wind scatters dust and other things. One says "ذَرَتِ الرِّيحُ" and "أذْرَتْ" with one meaning: "ذَرَتْ، فَهي ذارِيَةٌ، وهُنَّ ذارِياتٌ", and "أذْرَتْ، فَهي مُذْرِيَةٌ" and "مُذْرِياتٌ" for the plural, and "ذارِياتٌ" as well. The meaning is: "By the Lord of the scattering winds, the Lord of the running ships, and the Lord of the apportioning angels, what you are promised is true."

zajjaj:10-10.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُتِلَ الخَرّاصُونَ﴾: they are the liars; you say: "قَدْ تَخَرَّصَ عَلَيَّ فُلانٌ الباطِلَ" (so-and-so fabricated falsehood against me). It is also possible that "اَلْخَرّاصُونَ" are those who conjecture something without establishing it, and so act on what they do not know to be sound.

zajjaj:12-12.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَسْألُونَ أيّانَ يَوْمُ الدِّينِ﴾ — and "إيّانَ" is permissible, with kasra on the hamza as well as with fatḥa — that is: they say: when is the Day of Recompense?

zajjaj:13-13.t:
His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ هم عَلى النّارِ يُفْتَنُونَ﴾, with "يَوْمَ" in the accusative; and "يَوْمُ هم عَلى النّارِ يُفْتَنُونَ" (nominative) is permissible. Whoever puts it in the accusative, it is in two ways. One of them is in the sense of: "the recompense will occur on the day they are tried over the Fire". It is also possible that its form is the form of the accusative while its sense is the sense of the nominative, because it is in iḍāfa (annexed) to a whole clause. You say: "يُعْجِبُنِي يَوْمَ أنْتَ قائِمٌ" (the day you are standing pleases me), "يَوْمُ أنْتَ قائِمٌ" and "يَوْمُ أنْتَ تَقُومُ"; and if you wish you give it fatḥa while it is in the position of the nominative, as the poet said:
؎لَمْ يَمْنَعِ الشُّرْبَ مِنها غَيْرَ أنْ نَطَقَتْ ∗∗∗ حَمامَةٌ في غُصُونٍ ذاتِ أوْقالِ
(Nothing kept her from drinking but that a dove cooed among branches bearing dry fruit.)
It has also been transmitted as "غَيْرُ أنْ نَطَقَتْ". When he annexed "غَيْرُ" to "أنْ", which is not fully declinable (mutamakkin), it took fatḥa; likewise when "يَوْمُ" was annexed to "هم عَلى النّارِ", it took fatḥa. And as it has been read: "وَمِن خِزْيِ يَوْمَئْذٍ", where you give "يَوْمَ" fatḥa while it is in the position of the genitive, because you have annexed it to something not fully declinable. The meaning of ﴿يُفْتَنُونَ﴾ is: they are burned and punished. From that the black stones that look as though they have been burned by fire are called "اَلْفَتِينُ".

zajjaj:15-15.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنَّ المُتَّقِينَ في جَنّاتٍ وعُيُونٍ﴾ ﴿آخِذِينَ ما آتاهم رَبُّهُمْ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 16]: He, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known what the people of the Fire will have, then made known what the people of the Garden will have; because when He said: ﴿وَإنَّ الدِّينَ لَواقِعٌ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 6], He made known the recompense of the people of the Garden and the recompense of the people of the Fire.
His saying: ﴿آخِذِينَ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 16] is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). The meaning is: "the God-fearing are in gardens and springs, in the state of taking what their Lord has given them". Were it outside the Qur'an, "آخِذُونَ" (nominative) would be permissible, but the Muṣḥaf is not to be contradicted; the meaning would then be: "the God-fearing are taking what their Lord has given them, in gardens and springs". The first aspect is better in meaning, and the reading is according to it.

zajjaj:17-17.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كانُوا قَلِيلا مِنَ اللَّيْلِ ما يَهْجَعُونَ﴾: the meaning is: "they used to slumber a little of the night", that is: "they used to sleep a little of the night". Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known in what their wakefulness consisted, and said: ﴿وَبِالأسْحارِ هم يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 18]. It is possible that "ما" is emphatic, redundant (laghw); and it is possible that "ما" with what follows it is a maṣdar (verbal noun; i.e. an interpreted maṣdar), so that the meaning is: "little of the night was their slumber".

zajjaj:19-19.t: ﴿وَفِي أمْوالِهِمْ حَقٌّ لِلسّائِلِ والمَحْرُومِ﴾: "اَلْمَحْرُومُ" (the deprived): it has come in the tafsīr (exegesis): the one whose wealth does not grow (lā yanmū); and more common in the language is lā yanmī lahu māl. It has also come that he is "اَلْمُجازِفُ" (the venturer), who scarcely earns anything.

zajjaj:23-23.t: His saying: ﴿فَوَرَبِّ السَّماءِ والأرْضِ إنَّهُ لَحَقٌّ﴾, that is: "what the Prophet ﷺ brought is true, and His saying ﴿وَفِي السَّماءِ رِزْقُكم وما تُوعَدُونَ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 22] is true". So the meaning is that what we have mentioned concerning the signs, provision and the affair of the Prophet ﷺ is true, ﴿مِثْلَ ما أنَّكم تَنْطِقُونَ﴾ — and it has been read "مِثْلُ ما أنَّكم تَنْطِقُونَ" (nominative). This is as you say in ordinary speech: "إنَّ هَذا لَحَقٌّ، كَما أنَّكَ مُتَكَلِّمٌ" (this is surely true, just as you are speaking). Whoever puts "مِثْلُ" in the nominative, it is a ṣifa (adjective) of al-ḥaqq, the meaning being: "it is surely a truth like your speaking". Whoever puts it in the accusative, it is of two kinds. One of them is that it is in the position of the nominative, except that, when it was annexed to "أنَّ", it took fatḥa. It is also possible that it is accusative for emphasis (tawkīd), in the sense of: "it is surely true, truly, like your speaking".

zajjaj:24-24.t: His saying: ﴿هَلْ أتاكَ حَدِيثُ ضَيْفِ إبْراهِيمَ المُكْرَمِينَ﴾: It has come in the tafsīr (exegesis) that when the angels came to him, he honoured them with the calf. It was also said: he honoured them by serving them himself — the blessings of Allah be upon him and upon them.

zajjaj:25-25.t:
﴿فَقالُوا سَلامًا قالَ سَلامٌ﴾ — and it has been read: "قالَ سِلْمٌ". The accusative of the first is in the sense of "peace be upon you, a greeting of peace" and "we greet you with a greeting of peace". Whoever reads ﴿قالَ سَلامٌ﴾, it is in two ways: in the sense of "he said: peace be upon you", and it is possible that it is in the sense of "our affair is peace". Whoever reads "سِلْمٌ", the meaning is: "he said: peace", that is: "my affair is peace" and "our affair is peace", that is: "there is no harm upon us".
His saying: ﴿قَوْمٌ مُنْكَرُونَ﴾: its nominative is in the sense of: "you are a people unknown".

zajjaj:26-26.t: ﴿فَراغَ إلى أهْلِهِ فَجاءَ بِعِجْلٍ سَمِينٍ﴾: the meaning of ﴿فَراغَ إلى أهْلِهِ﴾ is: he turned aside to them in such a way that they did not know why he had turned aside. Likewise one says: "راغَ فُلانٌ عَنّا" (so-and-so slipped away from us) when he turns away from them without their knowing.

zajjaj:27-27.t: His saying: ﴿فَقَرَّبَهُ إلَيْهِمْ قالَ ألا تَأْكُلُونَ﴾: the meaning is: "he brought it near to them so that they might eat of it, but they did not eat; he said: Will you not eat?!", as a disapproval, that is: "your conduct in not eating is something I find strange."

zajjaj:28-28.t:
His saying: ﴿فَأوْجَسَ مِنهم خِيفَةً قالُوا لا تَخَفْ﴾: the meaning of "أوْجَسَ" is: fear arose in his soul.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَبَشَّرُوهُ بِغُلامٍ عَلِيمٍ﴾: the meaning of "عَلِيمٍ" is that he will reach maturity and know.

zajjaj:29-29.t:
His saying: ﴿فَأقْبَلَتِ امْرَأتُهُ في صَرَّةٍ﴾: "اَلصَّرَّةُ" here is intense crying out. ﴿فَصَكَّتْ وجْهَها﴾, that is: she struck her face.
﴿وَقالَتْ عَجُوزٌ عَقِيمٌ﴾: the meaning is: "she said: I am a barren old woman, so how shall I give birth?!" The proof of that is His saying in another place: ﴿قالَتْ يا ويْلَتى أألِدُ وأنا عَجُوزٌ وهَذا بَعْلِي شَيْخًا﴾ [Hūd: 72]

zajjaj:30-30.t: ﴿قالُوا كَذَلِكَ قالَ رَبُّكِ﴾, that is: as we have said to you, so your Lord has said; that is: "we are only informing you on behalf of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, and Allah is Wise, Knowing; He is able to make the barren one fertile, and the old woman likewise." So Abraham knew that they were messengers and that they were angels.

zajjaj:31-31.t: ﴿قالَ فَما خَطْبُكم أيُّها المُرْسَلُونَ﴾, that is: "what is your business? And for what have you been sent?"

zajjaj:32-32.t:
﴿قالُوا إنّا أُرْسِلْنا إلى قَوْمٍ مُجْرِمِينَ﴾ ﴿لِنُرْسِلَ عَلَيْهِمْ حِجارَةً مِن طِينٍ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 33], that is: "we have been sent to a criminal people to destroy them for their disbelief.
[Translator's note: the opening quotation mark in the source is not closed.]

zajjaj:34-34.t: ﴿مُسَوَّمَةً عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ لِلْمُسْرِفِينَ﴾, that is: marked; on every stone of them is the name of the one whose destruction was appointed by it. "اَلْمُسَوَّمَةُ" is the marked one, taken from "اَلسُّومَةُ", which is the mark.

zajjaj:6-6.t: His saying: ﴿وَإنَّ الدِّينَ لَواقِعٌ﴾, that is: "the recompense for your deeds will surely come to pass".

zajjaj:7-7.t:
His saying: ﴿والسَّماءِ ذاتِ الحُبُكِ﴾ ﴿إنَّكم لَفي قَوْلٍ مُخْتَلِفٍ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 8]: It has come in the tafsīr (exegesis) that it is the one possessing good khuluq. [Translator's note: the source reads «الخُلُقِ» (character); «الخَلْقِ» (form, make) is likely intended.] The people of the language say: "ذاتِ الحُبُكِ" means possessing fine pathways. "اَلْمَحْبُوكُ" in the language is that whose making is done well; and every [pattern of] pathways you see in water and in sand when the wind strikes it is "حُبُكٌ". Its singular is "حِباكٌ", like "مِثالٌ" and "مُثُلٌ"; and its singular may also be "حَبِيكَةٌ", like "طَرِيقَةٌ" and "طُرُقٌ".
His saying: ﴿إنَّكم لَفي قَوْلٍ مُخْتَلِفٍ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 8], that is: concerning the affair of the Prophet ﷺ.

zajjaj:9-9.t: ﴿يُؤْفَكُ عَنْهُ مَن أُفِكَ﴾, that is: turned away from it is whoever is turned away.

zajjaj:37-37.t: His saying: ﴿وَتَرَكْنا فِيها آيَةً لِلَّذِينَ يَخافُونَ العَذابَ الألِيمَ﴾, that is: We left in the city of the people of Lot a sign for those who fear, showing them that Allah destroyed them, so that others might be deterred from doing what they did.

zajjaj:38-38.t:
His saying: ﴿وَفِي مُوسى إذْ أرْسَلْناهُ إلى فِرْعَوْنَ بِسُلْطانٍ مُبِينٍ﴾: this is conjoined (ʿaṭf) to His saying: ﴿وَفِي الأرْضِ آياتٌ لِلْمُوقِنِينَ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 20], and to His saying: ﴿وَتَرَكْنا فِيها آيَةً لِلَّذِينَ يَخافُونَ العَذابَ الألِيمَ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 37].
His saying: ﴿بِسُلْطانٍ مُبِينٍ﴾, that is: with a clear proof.

zajjaj:39-39.t: ﴿فَتَوَلّى بِرُكْنِهِ﴾, that is: he turned away with that by which he strengthened himself, of his troops and his dominion. ﴿وَقالَ ساحِرٌ أوْ مَجْنُونٌ﴾: the meaning is: "and he said: this is a sorcerer or a madman".

zajjaj:40-40.t: ﴿فَأخَذْناهُ وجُنُودَهُ فَنَبَذْناهم في اليَمِّ﴾: "So We seized him and his support by which he strengthened himself". ﴿فَنَبَذْناهم في اليَمِّ﴾: "اَلْيَمُّ" is the sea. ﴿وَهُوَ مُلِيمٌ﴾, that is: blame clings to him; that is: what was done to him is not an expiation for him. "اَلْمُلِيمُ" in the language is one who does what he deserves to be blamed for. The meaning of "نَبَذْناهم" is: We cast them; everything you cast away you say of it: "قَدْ نَبَذْتُهُ" (I have cast it). From that is "نَبَذْتُ النَّبِيذَ" (I steeped the nabīdh), and from that you call a foundling "مَنبُوذٌ", because he has been thrown away.

zajjaj:41-41.t: His saying: ﴿وَفِي عادٍ إذْ أرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِمُ الرِّيحَ العَقِيمَ﴾, that is: "and in ʿĀd too there is a sign", according to what we explained concerning His saying ﴿وَفِي مُوسى﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 38]. The barren wind is the one with which there is no fertilisation, that is: it does not bring rain; it is only a wind of destruction.

zajjaj:42-42.t: ﴿ما تَذَرُ مِن شَيْءٍ أتَتْ عَلَيْهِ إلا جَعَلَتْهُ كالرَّمِيمِ﴾: "اَلرَّمِيمُ" is dry, crumbled leaves, like hashīm (dry stubble), as He said: ﴿كَهَشِيمِ المُحْتَظِرِ﴾ [al-Qamar: 31]

zajjaj:43-43.t: ﴿وَفِي ثَمُودَ﴾, that is: and in Thamūd too there is a sign.

zajjaj:46-46.t: His saying: ﴿وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ مِن قَبْلُ﴾: it has been read "وَقَوْمِ نُوحٍ" in the genitive and "وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ" in the accusative. Whoever puts it in the genitive, the meaning is: "and in the people of Noah". Whoever puts it in the accusative, it is conjoined to the sense of His saying: ﴿فَأخَذَتْهُمُ الصّاعِقَةُ وهم يَنْظُرُونَ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 44]; the meaning of "أخَذَتْهُمُ الصّاعِقَةُ" is: We destroyed them, so the meaning is: "We destroyed them, and We destroyed the people of Noah before". The better — and Allah knows best — is that it be construed on His saying: ﴿فَأخَذْناهُ وجُنُودَهُ فَنَبَذْناهم في اليَمِّ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 40], because the meaning is: "We drowned him and his troops, and We drowned the people of Noah before".

zajjaj:47-47.t: ﴿والسَّماءَ بَنَيْناها بِأيْدٍ﴾, that is: with strength. ﴿وَإنّا لَمُوسِعُونَ﴾: We have made between it and the earth an expanse.

zajjaj:48-48.t: ﴿والأرْضَ فَرَشْناها﴾ is conjoined to what precedes it, accusative by an implied (muḍmar) verb; the meaning is: "and We spread the earth — We spread it". The meaning of ﴿فَنِعْمَ الماهِدُونَ﴾ is "[excellent spreaders are] We", but the wording in His saying "فَرَشْناها" indicates the implied, omitted element.

zajjaj:49-49.t: His saying: ﴿وَمِن كُلِّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقْنا زَوْجَيْنِ﴾: the meaning — and Allah knows best — relates to animals, because the male and the female are called "زَوْجانِ" (a pair); like it is ﴿وَأنَّهُ خَلَقَ الزَّوْجَيْنِ الذَّكَرَ والأُنْثى﴾ [al-Najm: 45]. It is also possible that the pair is from every thing, so that the meaning is: "in every thing — in animals the male and the female", and in other than them "two kinds, the origin of every living and lifeless thing" — and Allah knows best.

zajjaj:50-50.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَفِرُّوا إلى اللَّهِ﴾: the meaning is: "so flee to Allah from associating partners with Allah and from disobeying Him, to Him". ﴿إنِّي لَكم مِنهُ نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ﴾, that is: "I warn you of His punishment and His penalty".

zajjaj:51-51.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلا تَجْعَلُوا مَعَ اللَّهِ إلَهًا آخَرَ إنِّي لَكم مِنهُ نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ ﴿كَذَلِكَ ما أتى الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ مِن رَسُولٍ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 52]: the meaning is: "the matter is thus", that is: as those before them did in denying the messengers.
﴿إلا قالُوا ساحِرٌ أوْ مَجْنُونٌ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 52], that is: "but they said: this is a sorcerer". "ساحِرٌ" is nominative by an implied "هُوَ" (he).

zajjaj:53-53.t: His saying: ﴿أتَواصَوْا بِهِ﴾: its meaning is: the first of them enjoined it upon the last of them. This is the alif of rebuke and the alif of interrogation.

zajjaj:54-54.t: His saying: ﴿فَتَوَلَّ عَنْهم فَما أنْتَ بِمَلُومٍ﴾, that is: "there is no blame upon you, since you have delivered the message".

zajjaj:55-55.t: ﴿وَذَكِّرْ فَإنَّ الذِّكْرى تَنْفَعُ المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾, that is: remind them of the days of Allah, His punishment, His penalty and His mercy.

zajjaj:56-56.t: His saying: ﴿وَما خَلَقْتُ الجِنَّ والإنْسَ إلا لِيَعْبُدُونِ﴾: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, knew before He created the jinn and mankind who would worship Him, as distinct from those who would disbelieve in Him. Had He created them only to compel them to worship Him, they would all have been worshipping believers, and there would have been none among them who went astray and disbelieved. So the meaning is: "I did not create the jinn and mankind except to call them to My worship, and I will worship from them" — meaning from those who are its people.

zajjaj:57-57.t: ﴿ما أُرِيدُ مِنهم مِن رِزْقٍ وما أُرِيدُ أنْ يُطْعِمُونِ﴾, that is: I do not want them to provide for any of My servants, nor do I want them to feed him, because I am the Provider, the One who feeds.

zajjaj:58-58.t: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ هو الرَّزّاقُ ذُو القُوَّةِ المَتِينُ﴾: the reading is the nominative, and in Arabic it is better, with "اَلْمَتِينُ" being nominative as a ṣifa (adjective) of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. Whoever reads "ذُو القُوَّةِ المَتِينِ", in the genitive, makes "اَلْمَتِينِ" a ṣifa of al-quwwa (strength), because the femininity of al-quwwa is like the femininity of al-mawʿiẓa, as He said: ﴿فَمَن جاءَهُ مَوْعِظَةٌ﴾ [al-Baqara: 275], the meaning being: "whoever has received an admonition (waʿẓ)". The meaning of ﴿ذُو القُوَّةِ المَتِينُ﴾ is: Possessor of intense power.

zajjaj:59-59.t:
His saying: ﴿فَإنَّ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا ذَنُوبًا مِثْلَ ذَنُوبِ أصْحابِهِمْ﴾: "اَلذَّنُوبُ" in the language is a share, and the bucket is called "اَلذَّنُوبُ". The meaning is: "those who have done wrong will have a share of punishment like the share of their companions who were destroyed, such as ʿĀd, Thamūd and the people of Lot.
﴿فَلا يَسْتَعْجِلُونِ﴾, that is: "if they are deferred until the Day of Resurrection".
[Translator's note: the quotation marks in the source are not balanced here.]

zajjaj:60-60.t: ﴿فَوَيْلٌ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِن يَوْمِهِمُ الَّذِي يُوعَدُونَ﴾, that is: from the Day of Resurrection.
